title: TSMC (TSM) Stock Price Prediction: Selloff meets a crowded bearish technical setup, but analyst targets and October revenue keep the longer case intact - Blockchain News
content: TSMC (TSM) closed at $343.76 on November 19, 2026, after a 5.57% daily drop, with the stock now sitting well below its short- and medium-term moving averages. At the same time, TSMC reported Octobe... TSMC (TSM) is trading through a sharp pullback: the stock finished at $343.76, down 5.57% on the day, with a 24-hour range of $375.39 to $339.43. The move leaves TSM well under its 7-day, 20-day, 50-day and 200-day moving averages, which is the kind of alignment traders usually read as a strong short-term trend break rather than a routine dip. That price action matters because it is happening against a still-firm operating backdrop. TSMC said October 2026 revenue came in at NT$586.89 billion, up 14.7% from September and 59.7% from a year earlier, while January-through-October revenue rose 43.3% year over year. Those numbers do not fix the stock’s tape, but they do argue against a demand collapse narrative. On November 19, Susquehanna kept its Buy rating and $600 target on TSMC, according to TIKR, calling out the selloff as overdone relative to the company’s longer-run earnings power. Bernstein also raised its TSMC target to $600 from $554 and kept an Outperform rating, according to the ad hoc report citing Stockrow, pointing to custom-chip demand from Amazon and Google and TSMC’s 2-nanometer roadmap. Across the broader analyst set quoted by Stockanalysis and TipRanks, sentiment remains positive: Stockanalysis showed a consensus Strong Buy with an average target of $586.69 from 21 analysts, while TipRanks showed a Strong Buy consensus from 9 analysts with an average target of $563.75. The range is wide, but the direction of travel is consistent: analysts are still leaning higher than the current quote. The setup is bearish on trend, but stretched on momentum. TSMC’s SMA stack is inverted, with the 7-day average at $372.20, the 20-day at $385.61, the 50-day at $417.49 and the 200-day at $423.36. The stock is also trading below the 12-day EMA of $376.07 and the 26-day EMA of $391.09, which reinforces the idea that sellers currently control the intermediate trend. Momentum is washed out rather than cleanly bearish. The daily RSI is 31.16, just above classic oversold territory, and the stochastic readings are extremely depressed at 5.44 for %K and 4.35 for %D. Bollinger positioning also shows price near the lower band at $346.22, with %B at -0.0312, which suggests the stock is pressing the lower edge of its recent volatility envelope. Support and resistance are clear. Immediate support sits at $330.33, with stronger support at $316.90. On the upside, the first meaningful test is $366.29, then $388.82. The pivot point at $352.86 is the key near-term line traders will watch to see whether the tape can stabilize or merely bounce within a broader downtrend. Binance perpetual futures show a split that does not line up neatly with the spot selloff. Funding is slightly positive at 0.0056%, which is neutral in practice. Open interest fell 5.65% over 24 hours to $14.5 million in notional terms, suggesting position reduction rather than fresh aggressive leverage. The long/short ratios are skewed long: global accounts are 72.0% long versus 28.0% short, and top-trader accounts are 79.9% long versus 20.1% short. That does not prove conviction in the equity itself, but it does show that Binance cohort positioning is leaning to the long side even as the price weakens. Taker flow is close to balanced at 0.9444, with buy volume of 1,202 versus sell volume of 1,273, so there is no strong intraday imbalance to confirm a reversal yet. The key invalidation for the bearish technical case is a recovery back above the pivot at $352.86 and then a reclaim of $366.29. That would not erase the broader damage, but it would signal that the stock is trying to build a base rather than extending the downtrend. Failure to hold $330.33 would expose $316.90, and a clean break below that level would keep the pressure on the stock even if analyst targets remain high. For now, TSMC’s fundamentals and Street targets are still constructive, but the chart says the market is demanding proof. title: Cups & Cakes in Rumson, NJ makes everything fresh daily, from custom cakes and more - New Jersey 101.5
content: There's a difference between your typical local spot, and that local spot where everybody knows your name. And earlier this week, that's exactly what I experienced when I paid a visit to Cups & Cakes in Rumson, NJ. Just the setting alone paints the picture of a unique small town bakery where all the locals frequent. But to actually hear customers talk with the staff as if they were long time friends is rare. However, that kind of interaction is not rare in a place like Cups & Cakes. And it's exactly the kind of atmosphere Denise, the owner, set out for going back to 2010 when they first opened their doors. From the moment I walked in, Denise was deep in conversation with a customer that you would swear are good friends or family members. It was very refreshing to say the least. And that was before I even had a chance to meet Denise to check out her store. It was quite the first impression, and one that you'll notice immediately from the first time you walk through the doors. Denise and the crew take pride in serving the community and creating all the custom cakes, cookies, and desserts they're known for. But it's so much more than that. They've got breakfast sandwiches, a juice bar, coffees, just to mention a few. All of it is amazing and just as good as the desserts. Speaking of which, they make everything fresh, everyday. One thing that stood out to me was when Denise shared what they do with their leftover food. They freeze it and donate it to numerous local soup kitchens in the area. I absolutely love that and can see why Denise is so loved in the community. Cups & Cakes in Rumson is looking for your vote to help crown them the champion in this years Jersey Shore Dessert Wars.
